artifacts.summary: Confirms the reconcile-path escape mechanism (temporally-pre-existing vs. causally-attributable baseline blind spot, not count-vs-identity), refutes the count-based-comparison premise, establishes provides.scripts is uncurated (safe to automate), and finds provides.agents/commands/context lack any equivalent disk-driven check.

memory_candidates.content: This repo's orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh and command-gate-out.sh share a baseline-tolerance philosophy (scripts/lib/deploy-baseline-lib.sh) that classifies a verify-deploy.sh finding as 'temporally pre-existing' (non-blocking) whenever it is present in BOTH a pre-redeploy and post-redeploy snapshot taken within the SAME checkpoint invocation. For any check whose subject lives purely in the source store (e.g. check-extension-docs.sh Rule Q, undeclared scripts), the source store does not change between those two snapshots, so a defect committed in an earlier cycle is ALWAYS 'temporally pre-existing' from this checkpoint's perspective -- even when it is 100% caused by the very task the checkpoint's reconcile pass is about to mark COMPLETED. The existing confirmation/attribution filter pair is applied only to the 'candidate new' branch, never to this pre-existing branch, so self-caused source-store defects structurally escape detection at completion time regardless of whether the pre/post comparison is count-based or identity-based (it is already identity-based, comm -13 over FINDING lines, since 2026-10-03).

check-extension-docs.sh has a disk-driven, pre-deploy 'undeclared file' check for provides.scripts (Rule Q), provides.rules (Rule H), and provides.skills (Rule A) -- but NOT for provides.agents, provides.commands, or provides.context. Those three categories only have a post-deploy 'orphan' check (Rules J/K/L), which is structurally blind to a file that was never declared in the first place (an undeclared file never deploys, so there is no orphan to find). A new, unregistered agent/command/context file has no gate anywhere in the lifecycle today, not even a mid-implementation catch.
